scope_limitations: PASS_KNOWN_SPEAR_HISTORY means all in-scope known SPEAR data-role references are resolved and their original TRAIN groups are excluded. It does not certify that candidate data were never seen by the whole project, previous v6 training, unrelated experiments, or unrecorded processes.

The plan scan covers the 37 existing spear*/**/plan.json files under the archived reproduction root. The access scan covers 25 archived non-test JSON ledger files and 12 current results JSON ledger/access files discovered at audit time.

Historical plan references that used /home/mizhou/JCAS/record/reproduction were resolved to existing byte-preserving archive paths. Every source path in this report is an existing absolute metadata-file path bound by its actual SHA256.

Only JSON/CSV/description metadata were inspected. No graph arrays, model weights, normalizer arrays or test results were loaded. Binary artifact references were deliberately not validated because this audit concerns data-role and identity provenance.

The historical formal-evaluation graph_access.csv mixes val/test accesses and was deliberately not opened. Test result/ledger paths were excluded, and test-key branches of formal plan metadata were skipped. This audit's exclusion lists concern original TRAIN groups.

Plan row-mention and ledger-entry totals include repeated roles across nested plans, multiple runs and byte-preserving current/archive copies; they are not independent observations. Excluded IDs are sorted and deduplicated.

Trace and checkpoint-AUC directories have no per-scene read ledger in the inspected records. Their scope is attributed using hash-bound parent roles, identical input contracts and matching replay/target identities; this is metadata provenance evidence, not an operating-system access audit.

A whole split_group_id is excluded whenever an in-scope original TRAIN scenario belongs to it. The excluded_scenario_ids list records known used scenes; it does not enumerate every sibling scene removed by group exclusion.
Candidate counts describe available graph metadata after group exclusion. Eligibility, later sample selection and confirmatory evaluation are separate from this history audit.
